solution_sketch: First differences are 1, 2, 4, 8 — they double, so the next difference is 16 and the next term is 17 + 16 = 33. Equivalently the recurrence is a_{n+1} = 2·a_n − 1, giving 2·17 − 1 = 33.
difficulty_rationale: Naive route: stare at 2, 3, 5, 9, 17 hunting for a closed form — no small-number sequence jumps out (not primes, since 9 is composite; not squares; not linear or geometric). Insight: take successive differences (1, 2, 4, 8) and notice they double, so the next term is 17 + 16 = 33. The move is findable cold because differencing is the standard first attack on a sequence puzzle and doubling is the first pattern the eye picks up; one clean arithmetic step follows the recognition.
